title: service-print: every server print fails under the console's default CSP, because the Chromium driver waits with a string predicate that needs 'unsafe-eval'
body:
Filing gate: ① a defect with a named landing. Found while landing #26583 (PR #26662, os-dev-report `6441342414`, `out_of_scope_findings` class a). Filed by the `domain:server` seat 1 (`session_01R1q2xdtYgU6FKrZ7LgjPCC`). ⛔ Not a claim. Dedupe: objectstack issues, all states, for "service-print CSP unsafe-eval waitForFunction", "print engine failed EvalError Content Security Policy" and "PRINT_READY_PREDICATE": no match.

**What fails.** On a default deployment every server print fails. `POST /api/v1/print/records` (and `printRecordToFile`) answers with "The print engine failed at the local executable …: page.waitForFunction: EvalError: Evaluating a string as JavaScript violates the following Content Security Policy directive …".

**Why.** `packages/services/service-print/src/chromium-driver.ts:303` waits for the page with `page.waitForFunction(PRINT_READY_PREDICATE, …)`, passing the predicate as a **string**. Evaluating a string needs `'unsafe-eval'`. The console's CSP (`packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts:851-852`) is `script-src 'self' 'nonce-…' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'` and adds `'unsafe-eval'` only when `OS_PAGE_REACT_ENABLED=true` (the `kind:'react'` page tier, off by default, ADR-0081).

**Measured** by the #26583 card thread on its head and on `main`'s untouched invoice leg of `packages/qa/dogfood/test/print-service-render.dogfood.test.ts` (real Chromium): with `OS_PAGE_REACT_ENABLED` unset, all 6 legs fail with the EvalError above; with `OS_PAGE_REACT_ENABLED=on`, all 8 pass. CI never saw it, because that file is `describe.skipIf(!CHROMIUM || !CONSOLE_BUILT)` and CI has no console bundle.

**Reach.** Every server-side print and PDF archive on a deployment that keeps the default CSP. It also blocks objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2312 (the quote print #26583 unblocks).

**Wanted.** The print driver's readiness wait works under the console's default CSP, without turning on `'unsafe-eval'`: for example a function argument (not a string) to `waitForFunction`, or a readiness signal the page sets itself, whichever the driver can run in the isolated world without eval. ⛔ Do not widen the console CSP for this. A test that runs the render under the default CSP should pin it, and CI's skip of the render dogfood is worth a look while there (a skipped render is not a passed one).

**Clause-②:** the dev measures it (likely `no`). **Metadata-protocol:** none expected.
